source_name: CBCG - Godišnji finansijski izvještaji sa izvještajem nezavisnog revizora (central bank's own audited accounts)
why_relevant: CBCG's own audited statements (2017-2024 published) disclose the central bank's auditor and its capitalised IT/payment-infrastructure spend - directly relevant to national payment-system modernisation (RTGS/DNS, SEPA, TIPS Clone) and the contractors behind it.

source_name: CBCG - Izvještaj o stabilnosti finansijskog sistema (Financial Stability Report)
why_relevant: Supervisory-analytical counterpart to Big-4/IFI assessments; sections on payment systems, digitalisation and operational/cyber risk describe infrastructure programmes and their state of play, providing the domestic baseline against which EC/IMF/EBRD statements can be triangulated.

source_name: European Commission - Montenegro Report (enlargement package SWD), financial services & digital chapters
why_relevant: Annual EC assessment (SWD(2025) 754 final) grades Montenegro on Chapter 4/9 financial services, payment-services alignment (PSD2), SEPA accession and digitalisation of public/financial services, naming legislative and infrastructure programmes and their timelines - the single most citable IFI-grade description of the modernisation agenda.

source_name: IMF - Montenegro country page, Article IV staff reports and concluding statements
why_relevant: 2024 and 2025 Article IV staff reports assess banking-system health and explicitly cover SEPA integration and TIPS Clone adoption - i.e. named national payment-infrastructure programmes; selected-issues papers and any FSAP-type annex specify supervisory IT and AML system requirements that translate into vendor demand.

source_name: IMF eLibrary - Montenegro Staff Country Reports series (structured archive)
why_relevant: Machine-readable/XML rendering of the same Article IV reports, easier to parse and to backfill a multi-year time series of statements about the payment system, bank IT and supervisory modernisation.

source_name: World Bank - Montenegro digital financial services / digital payments modernisation project
why_relevant: An EUR 8m World Bank loan to modernise Montenegro's digital payments infrastructure. IFI project documents (PAD, procurement plans, ISR) name components, implementing agencies and eventually awarded contractors - the most direct public route to identifying competitor vendors on a national payments programme.

source_name: EBRD - Montenegro country strategy, Transition Report and financial-institutions project summaries
why_relevant: EBRD is a lender/shareholder to Montenegrin banks and publishes country diagnostics, Transition Report chapters on digitalisation and project summary documents naming technical-assistance advisers and modernisation components. Also funds advisory (Advice for Small Businesses) engagements that reveal local consultancy ecosystem.

source_name: Credit rating agencies - sovereign and bank reports touching Montenegro (Moody's, S&P, Fitch)
why_relevant: Rating agency bank/sovereign reports and rating-action commentaries on Montenegro and on parent groups with ME subsidiaries (OTP, NLB, Erste, Addiko, Ziraat) discuss franchise digitalisation, cost-to-income and IT investment as rating drivers - competitor context that vendors never publish.

source_name: Ministarstvo finansija Crne Gore - Direktorat za ekonomsku politiku, banking sector analyses
why_relevant: Ministry of Finance economic-policy directorate bulletins quantify banking-sector performance and reference reform/modernisation programmes; they are the government-side counterpart that EC and IMF assessments draw on and often cite adviser-produced studies.

source_name: Government of Montenegro - Platforma ekonomskog oporavka 2022-2026 and successor reform programmes
why_relevant: National recovery/reform platforms set out digitalisation and financial-infrastructure measures with budgets and responsible institutions; these are the programme documents that IFI assessments then score, and they precede tenders.

source_name: Pilot Reform Monitor - Montenegro semester reports (independent reform tracking)
why_relevant: Independent analyst-layer tracking of Montenegro's EU Reform Agenda milestones, including digital and financial-sector measures; useful to date programme slippage that Big-4/IFI documents describe only in general terms.

source_name: Unija poslodavaca Crne Gore (Montenegrin Employers Federation) - studies on access to finance
why_relevant: Business-association commissioned studies on access to finance survey banks and SMEs, frequently produced with consultancy support; they profile bank product/channel capability from the demand side and identify the local consulting firms doing sector research.

source_name: Montenegro Business (monte.business) - English-language sector commentary on banking digitalisation
why_relevant: Secondary aggregator that summarises IMF/EC/CBCG findings on SEPA integration, mobile-banking growth and branch restructuring; useful as an early-warning pointer to the primary adviser/IFI documents rather than as evidence itself.

source_name: Zakon o reviziji / Zakon o kreditnim institucijama - statutory audit rules for banks (via CBCG legal repository)
why_relevant: Defines who may audit a credit institution (audit firm with at least two certified auditors with 3+ years of credit-institution audit experience; auditor must be selected by 30 September of the business year) and what the external auditor must report on, including information-system controls. Determines the cadence and content of the auditor-report stream and the small pool of eligible advisers.

source_name: Internet Archive Wayback Machine — CDX Server API (host-scoped snapshot enumeration for ME vendor/bank domains)
why_relevant: Only durable mechanism to recover deleted vendor reference/case-study pages and dead bank product pages (.me and regional vendor domains). Lets you enumerate every captured URL path for a host and diff over time, which surfaces 'reference/klijenti/rjesenja' pages that vendors removed after contracts ended.

source_name: Wayback Machine snapshot interface (per-URL time travel)
why_relevant: Retrieves the actual archived HTML of dead vendor case studies, bank e-banking product pages and tender annexes, i.e. the evidence itself rather than a pointer.

source_name: Službeni list Crne Gore — official gazette registry (registri)
why_relevant: Primary legal record: publishes CBCG decisions on payment systems (odluke o platnim sistemima, RTGS minimum value, incident reporting), the Zakon o platnom prometu and its amendments, plus government decisions establishing e-government/e-payment bodies. Gazette issue numbers are the durable citation anchor for any regulatory-driven procurement wave.

source_name: Paragraf.me — arhiva službenih glasila (Službeni list CG i opštinski propisi)
why_relevant: Commercial legal aggregator with a back-archive of gazette issues, including municipal-level acts. Useful fallback when sluzbenilist.me lacks older scans, and municipal acts reveal local e-payment / fiscalisation projects and their contractors.

source_name: PropisiNet.me — Zakon o platnom prometu (consolidated law with amendment history)
why_relevant: Consolidated text showing the amendment chain (62/2013, 6/2014, 111/2022, 7/2023, 15/2025). Each amendment wave is a leading indicator of bank IT/compliance procurement; the dates scope which archived vendor pages to hunt for.

source_name: CBCG — Platni promet i platni sistemi: podzakonski akti
why_relevant: Central bank's own index of secondary legislation on payment systems (nadzor nad platnim sistemima, RTGS thresholds, incident reporting 90/23). Defines the technical obligations banks must buy software to satisfy.

source_name: CBCG — Platni sistem (RTGS/DNS operator pages)
why_relevant: Describes the national payment system CBCG operates; historical snapshots of this page in Wayback reveal past system names/versions and, occasionally, the technology supplier behind RTGS/DNS modernisations.

source_name: CBCG — Arhiva (prinudna naplata / platni promet historical sections)
why_relevant: A native, regulator-maintained archive (year-indexed back to ~2006) — a rare case where the counterpart itself preserves superseded material, avoiding reliance on Wayback.

source_name: CBCG — Registar banaka (bank register, incl. historical/deregistered entities)
why_relevant: Canonical actor list for building the archive hunt: each current and former bank name/domain becomes a Wayback CDX target. Dead banks (merged/liquidated) are precisely the ones whose vendor evidence exists only in archives.

source_name: ePlaćanje — national e-payment portal for administrative taxes and fees
why_relevant: The live front end of the state e-payment scheme (NS NAT). Its card-acceptance chain (acquirer bank, PSP, 3-D Secure provider) is observable from the payment flow and page assets, identifying which payment vendor holds the state account — the reference win competitors will cite.

source_name: gov.me — 'Sistem za elektronsko plaćanje' (NS NAT description page)
why_relevant: Confirmed by fetch: names the system NS NAT, attributes it to Ministarstvo javne uprave, and links the companion control systems ekontrola.gov.me and provjeriuplate.gov.me. It does NOT name the implementer — which makes it a pointer into procurement records where the implementer is named.

source_name: Strategija digitalne transformacije Crne Gore 2022–2026 (PDF, MJU)
why_relevant: The state digital-agenda master document: lists planned information systems, e-payment/e-service workstreams, responsible institutions and indicative budgets — i.e. the forward pipeline of state IT and payment integrations that later become named contracts.

source_name: Uprava za javne nabavke / Direktorat za politiku javnih nabavki (ujn.gov.me) + elektronski sistem javnih nabavki (CEJN)
why_relevant: Where the implementers absent from strategy documents are actually named: tender notices, award decisions and contracts for state IT and e-payment systems. Also carries the public-procurement policy strategies (2011-2015, 2016-2020, 2021-2025) that frame IT spend.
